workspace_id_header.name: X-Workspace-Id
workspace_id_header.description: The numeric ID of the workspace you want to send a message in. This header is only needed when you authenticate with a service-account bearer token (`sa_live_…`). Service accounts work across workspaces, so you must supply this header so we know which workspace to send from. You can omit this header when you authenticate with a standard App API key, which is always scoped to one workspace.

object_type_id.name: object_type_id
object_type_id.description: The object type an object belongs to—like "Companies" or "Accounts". Object type IDs begin at `1` and increment for each new type.

object_id.name: object_id
object_id.description: The `object_id` or `cio_object_id` of an object, depending on the `id_type` specified in query params. `id_type` defaults to `object_id`.

suppression_type.name: suppression_type
suppression_type.description: The reason a person's email address was suppressed by the email service provider (ESP).

transactional_id.name: transactional_id
transactional_id.description: The identifier of your transactional message. You'll find this in the UI or URL of your transactional message. For example, if this is the path of a transactional message URL - `/transactional/3/templates/139` - the `transactional_id` is 3.

delivery_id.name: delivery_id
delivery_id.description: The delivery resulting in a request to unsubscribe.

activityTypes.name: type
activityTypes.description: The type of activity you want to search for. Types with `_o:<object_type_id>` are for objects and types with `_r:<object_type_id>` are for relationships.

sort.name: sort
sort.description: Determine how you want to sort results, `asc` for chronological order and `desc` for reverse chronological order.

activityName.name: name
activityName.description: The name of the event or attribute you want to return. For `consent` activities, the consent action, like `opted_in` or `opted_out`.

deleted.name: deleted
deleted.description: If true, return results for deleted people.

customer_id_query.name: customer_id
customer_id_query.description:
The `identifier` of the person you want to look up. By default, this is a person's `id`. You can use the `id_type` parameter to look up a person by `email`, `phone`, or `cio_id`.

If you use a person's `cio_id`, you must prefix the value with `cio_` when using it to find or reference a person (i.e. `cio_03000010` for a `cio_id` value of 03000010).

id_type.name: id_type
id_type.description: The type of `customer_id` you want to use to reference a person. If you don't provide this parameter, we assume that the `customer_id` in your request is a person's `id`. You can use `email` and `phone` only if they're enabled as identifiers in your [workspace settings](/accounts/workspaces/overview/#migrate-workspace); otherwise the request returns `400`. Reference `phone` values in [E.164 format](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E.164), like `+14155552671`, and URL-encode the leading `+` as `%2B`.

export_id.name: export_id
export_id.description: The export_id you want to access.

language-1.name: language
language-1.description: A [language tag](/journeys/channels/subscriptions/unsubscribe-faqs/#currently-supported-languages) you want the content translated in. If none is provided, the content will be sent in the default language of your subscription center.

language-2.name: language
language-2.description: A [language tag](/journeys/channels/subscriptions/unsubscribe-faqs/#currently-supported-languages) of a language variant. If you don't provide a language (an empty string), we'll use your default language. If the language variant does not exist, we'll return an error.

newsletter_id.name: newsletter_id
newsletter_id.description: The identifier of a one-time send.

content_id.name: content_id
content_id.description:
The identifier of a message in a one-time send. If your one-time send has an A/B test group or includes multiple languages, each variant has its own `content_id`, separate from the `newsletter_id`.

Use [List variants of a one-time send](/integrations/api/app/tag/newsletter-variants/listNewsletterVariants/) to find the `content_id` associated with the right variant.

campaign_id_query.name: campaign_id
campaign_id_query.description: The automation you want to filter for.

newsletter_id_query.name: newsletter_id
newsletter_id_query.description: The one-time send you want to filter for.

action_id_query.name: action_id
action_id_query.description: The action you want to filter for.

campaign_id.name: campaign_id
campaign_id.description: The ID of the automation that you want to trigger or return information about.

trigger_id.name: trigger_id
trigger_id.description: The ID of the automation trigger that you want to return information for.

track_customer_id.name: identifier
track_customer_id.description:
The unique value representing a person. The values you use to identify a person may be an `id`, `email` address, or the `cio_id` (when updating people), depending on your workspace settings. When you reference people by `cio_id`, you must prefix the value with `cio_`.

You can't reference a person by their `phone` number here. We determine the identifier type from the shape of the value, so a phone number in the path is treated as an `id`. To identify people by phone number, use the [Track v2 API](/integrations/api/track/tag/track_v2/).

oneOf.title: id
oneOf.description: The unique identifier for a person that you want to create or modify.

oneOf.title: email
oneOf.description: A person's email address. If adding a new person in an email-based workspace, you must use this value.

oneOf.title: cio_id
oneOf.description:
A canonical identifier assigned by Customer.io when you add a person. When referencing a person by this value, you must prefix the value with `cio_`. You can [look up a person using the App API](/integrations/api/app/tag/customers/) to find their `cio_id`.

You must use this value to update a person's other identifiers—their `id` or `email`, unless you enable your workspace's [Allow updates to email using ID](/accounts/workspaces#update-email-with-id) setting.

trackEvent_customer_id.name: identifier
trackEvent_customer_id.description: The unique value representing a person. You may identify a person by `id`, `email` address, or the `cio_id` (when updating people), depending on your workspace settings. You can't reference a person by their `phone` number here; a phone number in the path is treated as an `id`. To identify people by phone number, use the [Track v2 API](/integrations/api/track/tag/track_v2/).

oneOf.title: id
oneOf.description: The unique identifier you assigned to a person.

oneOf.title: email
oneOf.description: A person's email address.

oneOf.title: cio_id
oneOf.description:
A canonical identifier assigned by Customer.io when you add a person. When referencing a person by this value, you must prefix the value with `cio_`. You can [look up a person using the App API](/integrations/api/app/tag/customers/) to find their `cio_id`, but you must prefix this value with `cio_` when using it to reference a person.

You can use this value to update a person's other identifiers—their `id` or `email`.

customer_id.name: customer_id
customer_id.description: The ID of the customer you want to perform an operation against.

device_id.name: device_id
device_id.description: The ID of the device you want to perform an operation against.

segment_id.name: segment_id
segment_id.description: The identifier for a segment. You can find your segment's ID on its page in the dashboard—go to *Segments*, select your segment, and find the ID under *Usage*. Or you can find your segment using the [App API](/integrations/api/app/tag/segments/).

start.name: start
start.description: The token for the page of results you want to return. Responses contain a `next` property. Use this property as the `start` value to return the next page of results.

resolution.name: res
resolution.description: Determines increment for metrics—hourly, daily, weekly, or monthly.

journey_resolution.name: resolution
journey_resolution.description: Determines the increment for journey metrics—hourly, daily, weekly, or monthly.

limit.name: limit
limit.description: The maximum number of results you want to retrieve per page.

limit-10-100.name: limit
limit-10-100.description: The maximum number of results you want to retrieve per page.

limit-50-1000.name: limit
limit-50-1000.description: The maximum number of results you want to retrieve per page.

limit-100-1000.name: limit
limit-100-1000.description: The maximum number of results you want to retrieve per page.

offset.name: offset
offset.description: The number of records to skip before retrieving results.

action_id.name: action_id
action_id.description: The action you want to lookup or act on.

period.name: period
period.description: The unit of time for your report.

steps.name: steps
steps.description: The number of periods you want to return. Defaults to the maximum available, or `12` if the period is in `months`. Maximums are 24 hours, 45 days, 12 weeks, or 121 months. Days start at 00:00 EST. Weeks start at 00:00 EST on Sunday. Months start at 00:00 EST on the 1st of the month.

metricType.name: type
metricType.description: The type of item you want to return metrics for. When empty, the response contains metrics for all possible types.

newsletterMetricsType.name: type
newsletterMetricsType.description: The type of item you want to return metrics for. When empty, the response contains metrics for all possible types.

metric.name: metric
metric.description: Determines the metric(s) you want to return.

unique.name: unique
unique.description: If true, the response contains only unique customer results, i.e. a customer who clicks a link twice is only counted once. If false, the response contains the total number of results without regard to uniqueness.

drafts.name: drafts
drafts.description: If true, your request returns drafts rather than active/sent messages.

get_tracked_responses.name: get_tracked_responses
get_tracked_responses.description: If true, the response includes `tracked_responses` for each message—an object containing tracked response option names for in-app survey responses.

get_apitb_broadcast_id.name: broadcast_id
get_apitb_broadcast_id.description: The ID of the broadcast that you want to return information about.

start_ts.name: start_ts
start_ts.description: The beginning timestamp for your query.

end_ts.name: end_ts
end_ts.description: The ending timestamp for your query.

id_type_segment.name: id_type
id_type_segment.description: The type of `ids` you want to use. All of the values in the `ids` array must be of this type. If you don't provide this parameter, we assume that the `ids` array contains `id` values.

Page.name: page
Page.description: The page number of results you want to display. Use with `limit`.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: The maximum number of results per page.

DirectDescendantsOnly.name: direct_descendants_only
DirectDescendantsOnly.description: When `true`, the response includes only the immediate children of the parent folder. When `false`, it includes the parent folder's entire subtree.

asset-id.name: id
asset-id.description: The unique identifier of the resource.

AssetParentFolderID.name: parent_folder_id
AssetParentFolderID.description: Filter results to a specific parent folder. Use 0 or omit to target the root level.

email_id.name: id
email_id.description: The id of the email. If your email has multiple languages, you must provide the ID of the **default** language template. This links the workflow to all of the language variants for the template.

email_variant_id.name: id
email_variant_id.description: The UUID of the email. If your email has translations, this is the ID of a specific language variant.

whatsapp_id.name: id
whatsapp_id.description: The UUID of the WhatsApp template.

inbox_id.name: id
inbox_id.description: The UUID of the inbox message. If the message has multiple languages, you must provide the ID of the **default** language template. This links the workflow to all of the language variants for the template.

run_id.name: run_id
run_id.description: The ID of the inbox preview job, returned by [Send for inbox previews](/integrations/api/design-studio/tag/email-testing/submitInboxPreview/).

preview_client_id.name: client_id
preview_client_id.description: The device identifier for the capture, matching a value from `client_ids` in the response of [Send for inbox previews](/integrations/api/design-studio/tag/email-testing/submitInboxPreview/).

Language.name: language
Language.description: A [language code](/journeys/channels/localization/attribute/#supported-languages) that indicates the language of your translated email

ParentFolderID.name: parent_folder_id
ParentFolderID.description:
Filter by parent folder. Must reference an existing folder. If not set, the response filters by the root level directory.

To list only items in the root folder, leave `parent_folder_id` unset and only set `direct_descendants_only` to `true`.

CreatedBefore.name: created_before
CreatedBefore.description: Return records created before this time. Must be a unix timestamp.

CreatedAfter.name: created_after
CreatedAfter.description: Return records created after this time. Must be a unix timestamp.

UpdatedBefore.name: updated_before
UpdatedBefore.description: Return records updated before this time. Must be a unix timestamp.

UpdatedAfter.name: updated_after
UpdatedAfter.description: Return records updated after this time. Must be a unix timestamp.

anyType.description: Can be any type of value.

anonymous_id.description: An identifier for an anonymous event, like a cookie. If set as an attribute on a person, any events bearing the same anonymous value are associated with this person. This value must be unique and is not reusable.

cio_id.description: A unique identifier set by Customer.io, used to reference a person if you want to update their identifiers.

optoutChannels.description: The senders and channels that the person is opted out of. An entry's presence means the person is opted out of that sender on that channel.

channel.description: The channel that the person is opted out of.

from.description: The sender that the person is opted out of. For SMS, this is a sender phone number (E.164), an alphanumeric sender ID, or a messaging-service SID; for WhatsApp, it's the sender phone number.

bytes.description: The size of the collection in bytes.

id.description: The identifier for the collection. This is how you'll reference the collection from the API.

name.description: The name of the collection. This is how you'll reference the collection in liquid, e.g. `{{collection_name.data_property}}`.

rows.description: Represents the number of objects in the `data` array or CSV rows in your collection schema.

schema.description: Lists the top-level keys that you can reference within this collection. Customer.io does not enforce any of these keys as required from your `data`.

exportSharedProps.description: Contains properties shared by export filters.

attributes.description: Recipient attributes you want to include as extra columns in your export. You can't include event or trigger properties.

template_id.description: Restrict the export to a specific message template (content) within the selected automation, one-time send, or transactional message.

next.description: Indicates the next page of results. Add `?start=<next_value>` to the request to get the next page of results.

anonymousEventsRequest.description: An event attributed to an unknown person. If you provide an `anonymous_id` with the event, you can associate the event with a person later (using the anonymous ID).

name.description: The name of the event. This is how you'll reference the event in automations or segments.

type.description: Sets the event type. If your event isn't a `page` or `screen` type event, we automatically set this property to `event`.

timestamp.description: The unix timestamp when the event took place. If you don't provide this value, we use the date-time when we receive the event.

data.description: Additional event data you can reference in Liquid or use to set customer attributes. You can include `from_address` and `reply_to`, but an event only triggers an automation if you associate it with a person within 72 hours.

additionalProperties.description: Insert key-values that you want to reference in messages or convert to attributes if/when you associate this event with a person.

delivered.description: The date-time when the message was delivered, if applicable.

opened.description: Indicates whether or not a customer opened a message, if the message was delivered.

oneOf.title: Attribute change
oneOf.description: The name of the object is the attribute that changed.

oneOf.title: Consent record
oneOf.description: The data for a `consent` activity. The activity's `name` is the action, `opted_in` or `opted_out`. Customer.io fills in the optional fields when the change that created the record has that information. See [Consent records](/messaging/channels/subscriptions/consent-records/#what-a-record-contains).

consent_state.description: The state the change left the person in.

collection_point.description: Where the change came from, like your subscription center or an SMS reply. The `subscription_preference_migration` and `sender_optout_migration` values mark records that Customer.io imported from preferences and opt-outs that existed before your account recorded consent.

channel.description: The channel the consent applies to, like `email` or `sms`. Absent when the consent applies to all of your messages.

topic_id.description: The subscription topic the consent applies to, if any.

topic_name.description: The topic's name when the change happened. Renaming the topic later doesn't change this value.

sender_id.description: The sender identity the consent applies to, if any.

from.description: The sender's email address or phone number when the change happened.

delivery_id.description: The message the person responded to, like the email that contained the unsubscribe link.

received_on.description: The address or phone number the person's reply came from.

profile_identifier.description: The identifier your request used to find the person.

response.description: What the person sent back, like the body of an SMS reply.

source_event_id.description: The ID of the activity that produced this record, like the inbound SMS that contained STOP.

id.description: The identifier for the action.

timestamp.description: The date and time when the action occurred.

name.description: The name of the event, for `event` and `screen` activities. For `consent` activities, the consent action, which is `opted_in`, `opted_out`, or `voided`.

delivery_id.description: The instance of a message sent to a person.

activityTypes.description: The type of activity. Types with `_o:<object_type_id>` are for objects and types with `_r:<object_type_id>` are for relationships.

from.description: The old attribute value. If empty, the customer probably didn't bear the attribute before this action.

segmentAudienceFilter.title: segment
segmentAudienceFilter.description: Provide the `id` of a segment containing people you want to search for.

id.description: The ID of the segment you want to return people from.

inverse.description: Set to `true` to match people who *aren't* in the segment.

field.description: The name of the attribute you want to filter against.

operator.description: Determine how to evaluate criteria against the field—`exists` returns results if a person in the audience has the attribute; `eq` returns results if the audience has the attribute and the attribute has the `value` you specify.

value.description: The value you want to match for this attribute. You must include a value if you use the `eq` operator.

inverse.description: Set to `true` to match people who *don't* meet the condition.

anyOf.title: segment
anyOf.description: Filter for people who belong to a segment.

anyOf.title: audience
anyOf.description: filter for people who have an attribute or an attribute value.

complexAudienceFilter.title: People Filter
complexAudienceFilter.description: Filter people with `and`, `or`, and `not` groups made from `segment` and `attribute` conditions.

not.description: Returns people who don't match conditions. `not` takes a single object, not an array. That object can be one condition, or an `and` or `or` group when you want to exclude people who match a combination of conditions.

notAudienceFilter.title: not
notAudienceFilter.description: Returns people who don't match the condition inside it. `not` takes a single object, not an array. That object can be one condition, or an `and` or `or` group when you want to exclude people who match a combination of conditions.

audienceFilter.title: Audience Filter
audienceFilter.description: Use `and`, `or`, and `not` to combine segment and attribute conditions. The top-level object accepts one property; nest groups for complex filters.

oneOf.title: segment
oneOf.description: Filter for people who belong to a segment.

oneOf.title: audience
oneOf.description: filter for people who have an attribute or an attribute value.

objectattributeFilter.title: object attribute
objectattributeFilter.description: Filter your objects by their attributes.

field.description: The name of the attribute you want to filter against.

operator.description: Determine how to evaluate criteria against the field—`exists` returns results if an object has the attribute; `eq` returns results an object's attribute exists and the attribute has the `value` you specify.

value.description: The value you want to match for this attribute. You must include a value if you use the `eq` operator.

not.description: Returns results if a condition is false. While and/or support an array of items, `not` supports a single condition.

objectFilter.title: Object Filter
objectFilter.description: Use `and`, `or`, and `not` to combine object attribute conditions. The top-level object accepts one property; nest groups for complex filters.

oneOf.title: object attribute
oneOf.description: A simple filter to find objects matching an attribute condition.

device_object_common.description: Device information common to the v1 and v2 APIs.

last_used.description: The `timestamp` when you last identified this device. If you don't pass a timestamp when you add or update a device, we use the time of the request itself. Our SDKs identify a device when a person launches their app.

attributes.description: Attributes that you can reference to segment your audience—like a person's attributes, but specific to a device. These can be either the attributes defined below or custom key-value attributes.

device_os.description: The operating system, including the version, on the device.

device_model.description: The model of the device a person uses.

app_version.description: The version of your app that a customer uses. You might target app versions to let people know when they need to update, or expose them to new features when they do.

app_identifier.description: The app that the device belongs to—the **Bundle ID / App identifier** you entered with that app's push credentials. If you have more than one app, we use this attribute to send push notifications to the right app. A device without an app identifier receives push notifications you send to your [default app](/messaging/channels/push/getting-started/#the-default-app).

cio_sdk_version.description: The version of the Customer.io SDK in the app.

_last_status.description: The delivery status of the last message sent to the device—sent, bounced, or suppressed. An empty string indicates that that the device hasn't received a push yet.

device_locale.description: The device's [IETF language code](/journeys/channels/localization/getting-started/#supported-languages), such as `en-MX` or `es-ES`.

push_enabled.description: If `"true"`, the device is opted-in and can receive push notifications.

additionalProperties.description: Custom properties that you want to associate with the device.

recipients.description:
Filter conditions that define the one-time send's recipients. In `recipients`, you can combine `segment` and `attribute` conditions with `and`, `or`, and `not` operators.

This endpoint enforces a strict shape:

* The outermost object must be a single `and` array.
* Every operator or condition object takes exactly **one** key: `and`, `or`, `not`, `segment`, or `attribute`. An object with two keys—like `not` alongside `and`—is rejected with an "Invalid filter spec" error.
* Segment conditions must be wrapped in an `or` array, even for a single segment—and `or` arrays can contain only segment conditions.
* To exclude segments, `not` must contain an `or` of segment conditions and sit as its own item inside the `and` array.
* Attribute conditions sit directly in the `and` array, unwrapped. To negate an attribute condition, set `inverse: true` on the attribute itself—`not` can't contain attribute conditions.

The email example on this operation shows or-wrapped segments combined with a negated attribute; for the common "include segment A, exclude segment B" pattern, see the **include one segment, exclude another** request example. See [Format API-triggered broadcasts](/messaging/send/broadcasts/api-triggered-data-format/#overriding-recipients) for general operator behavior.

and.description: An array of conditions that must all be true.

or.description: An array of conditions where at least one must be true. On this endpoint, `or` arrays can contain only segment conditions.

not.description: A condition or group of conditions to exclude. On this endpoint, `not` must contain an `or` of segment conditions and sit as its own item inside the `and` array. An object with both `and` and `not` keys is rejected with an "Invalid filter spec" error.

id.description: The ID of a segment.

value.description: The value to compare against. Required when `operator` is `eq`.

inverse.description: Set to `true` for "is not equal" or "does not exist".

send_now.description: If `true`, the one-time send is sent immediately after creation. You cannot set both `send_now` and `scheduled_at`.

scheduled_at.description: A Unix timestamp indicating when to send the one-time send. The time must be in the future. You cannot set both `send_now` and `scheduled_at`.

subscription_topic_id.description: The one-time send audience's subscription topic ID. Required when [subscription center](/journeys/channels/subscriptions/center/#enable-sub-center) is enabled; otherwise sends to globally subscribed profiles.

recipient_file_url.description: A URL pointing to a CSV of recipients, used instead of the `recipients` filter. Customer.io resolves the file in the background, so this request can't also send or schedule. Poll [Get a one-time send](/integrations/api/app/tag/newsletters/getNewsletters/) until `recipient_file_status` is `done`, then call [send](/integrations/api/app/tag/send-messages/sendNewsletter/) or [schedule](/integrations/api/app/tag/send-messages/scheduleNewsletter/).

expires_after.description: A send window in seconds, or `0` for no expiry. Customer.io stops delivering the one-time send once the window closes, so a delayed message doesn't arrive when it's no longer useful. Set it here only alongside `send_now` or `scheduled_at`, because the window runs from the send. On a plain draft, set it on the [send](/integrations/api/app/tag/send-messages/sendNewsletter/) or [schedule](/integrations/api/app/tag/send-messages/scheduleNewsletter/) call instead.

tag_ids.description: The IDs of the tags you want to apply to the one-time send. Each tag must already exist.

deduped.description: When `true`, Customer.io sends only one message per email address or phone number, even when several profiles share it. Supported on `email`, `twilio`, and `sms` one-time sends. Leave it out to use the default for your workspace's identifier configuration. No endpoint changes this later, so set it here if you don't want the default.

inAppBodyJson.description:
JSON body content for the in-app message, as a stringified JSON object—a JSON string, not a nested object. It supports these fields:
- `message_id`—string, an identifier for the message
- `carta_content`—string, the message content markup from our in-app editor
- `display`—object; `mode` (`modal`, `overlay`, `inline`, or `tooltip`) and `value` (the position for modals: `top`, `center`, or `bottom`; the position ID for inline messages). Tooltips take a `tooltip_target` CSS selector instead of `value`
- `priority`—integer, delivery order for queued messages: `1` (low), `5` (medium), or `10` (high)
- `expiration`—object; if omitted, the message expires after 30 days (60 maximum). Set `type` (`relative` or `absolute`), `unit`, and `value`
- `persistent`—boolean, keep the message visible across pages and sessions until your audience dismisses it
- `attributes`—object, custom key-value string pairs delivered with the message
- `route_rules` and `excluded_route_rules`—objects keyed by platform (`web`, `ios`, or `android`), each holding an array of [page rules](/messaging/channels/in-app/send-in-app-message/#page-rule) with an `operator` (`contains` or `equals`), a `value` (`*` is a wildcard), and an `order` (integer). You can only set page rules when you create a message, and platforms you don't set rules for won't show the message

inboxBodyJson.description:
JSON body content for the inbox message, as a stringified JSON object. The fields you include depend on how you [set up your inbox](/journeys/channels/in-app/inbox/setup/):
- `topics`—array, topics your audience can filter by in their inbox
- `type`—string, context that helps render the inbox message
- `properties`—object, your message info like the title, body, link, and image
- `expiration`—object; if omitted, the message expires after 30 days. Otherwise set `type` (`relative` or `absolute`), `unit` (`seconds`, `minutes`, `hours`, or `days`; relative only), and `value` (number of units, or a unix timestamp if absolute)

rate_limit_email_rate.description: Maximum number of messages per time period. **NOTE:** Though this states `email_rate`, you can use this for other message channels. Only fixed rate limits are supported, not [daily ramp limits](/messaging/send/broadcasts/one-time-sends/#daily-ramp).

rate_limit_time_period.description: Time period in seconds for rate limiting. Must be one of 60 (minute), 3600 (hour), or 86400 (day).

rate_limit_spread.description: When `true`, spreads messages evenly across the time period. Otherwise, it sends as fast as possible up to the limit in each period.

newsletterScheduleRequest.description: Only `scheduled_at` is required. If you want to send with a rate limit, set both `rate_limit_email_rate` or `rate_limit_time_period`. `rate_limit_spread` can be set alone.

scheduled_at.description: Unix timestamp for the send. Use `0` to deschedule. When greater than `0`, the time must be in the future and you must send `timezone` so the UI displays the time correctly.

timezone.description: [IANA timezone name](/journeys/send/timezones/example-timezones/#region-format) (for example, `America/New_York`). Required when `scheduled_at` is greater than `0`. Not required when descheduling (`scheduled_at` is `0`).

tz_match_enabled.description: When `true`, sends at the same local time in each recipient's timezone. If it's set to `true` and `rate_limit_time_period` is provided, then the period can't be greater than `3600` (1 hour).

expires_after.description: A send window in seconds measured from the scheduled time, or `0` for no expiry. Customer.io stops delivering the one-time send once the window closes. You can't combine it with `tz_match_enabled`, with send time optimization, or with descheduling (`scheduled_at` of `0`), and on an A/B test it must outlast the test duration.

content_ids.description: A list of message variants in a one-time send, where a variant is a translation or A/B test.

name.description: The name of the one-time send. Must be 190 characters or less.

sent_at.description: The last time the one-time send was sent, or `null` if it hasn't been sent.

send_state.description:
Where the one-time send is in its lifecycle. Always included. This matches the status shown in Customer.io, with one exception noted under `awaiting_winner`.

- `drafted`: The one-time send isn't scheduled and hasn't been sent.
- `scheduled`: A send time is set and sending hasn't started.
- `sending`: Sending has started and is still in progress. More batches are due (timezone-match batches or the remainder of an A/B test), or messages are still being delivered.
- `sent`: The one-time send is no longer sending. This doesn't mean that every individual message has reached a final state.
- `paused`: The one-time send is paused.
- `stopped`: The one-time send was stopped.
- `failed`: The one-time send failed.
- `awaiting_winner`: An A/B test has started and is waiting for you to pick a winner before the rest of the audience gets it. Test messages might still be going out. Customer.io's UI stops showing "awaiting winner" 30 days after the first send, but the API keeps reporting `awaiting_winner` because you can still pick a winner.

When more than one state applies, Customer.io reports the first match in this order: `stopped`, `failed`, `paused`, `awaiting_winner`, `sending`, `sent`, `scheduled`, `drafted`.

scheduled_at.description:
When the one-time send is scheduled to go out, or `null` if it has no active schedule. Always included.

- A paused one-time send keeps its schedule, so this still has a value while `send_state` is `paused`.
- After sending starts, this stores the next scheduled send if there is one, like the next timezone batch or the remainder of an A/B test.
- When `tz_match_enabled` is `true`, the `scheduled_at` property is the time you asked for in the [schedule request](/integrations/api/app/tag/send-messages/scheduleNewsletter/) until sending starts.

id_ignore_missing.description: If false, a missing customer ID causes the broadcast to error and fail. If true, the broadcast will skip over any people in your audience who don't have IDs, and continue sending to the rest of your audience.

scheduled_at.description: Unix timestamp (in seconds) when the broadcast will send. Omit it or set it to `0` to send right away. We reject a timestamp more than 5 minutes in the past. Scheduling also changes when we work out your audience: `ids`, `emails`, `per_user_data`, and `data_file_url` set a fixed audience when you make this request, while a `recipients` filter runs when the send fires.

expires_after.description: Number of seconds after the send starts that the broadcast should stop sending. Omit or set to `0` if you don't want the broadcast to expire. A rate-limited send always expires: if you set `rate_limit` and omit this field or set it to `0`, we set it to 30 days. If the broadcast expires before it finishes sending, Customer.io discards the messages that haven't gone out yet instead of delivering them late. The window runs from `scheduled_at` when you schedule the send, and from the time we receive this request when you don't.

rate_limit.description: Lets people enter the broadcast at a fixed rate instead of all at the same time. For a broadcast with one message, this is the send rate. Later messages in a longer workflow follow your workflow and can go out faster. We determine your audience once, on the first run, and the trigger counts toward your queue limit until everyone enters, the send expires, or you cancel it. See [Limit the send rate](/messaging/send/broadcasts/api-triggered-broadcasts/#rate-limit).

rate.description: The maximum number of people that enter the broadcast in each `period`.

spread.description: When `true`, we let people in at an even pace across the period, once a minute or less often. When `false`, we let the full `rate` in at the start of each period.

deviceAttributeTriggerFilter.title: device attribute
deviceAttributeTriggerFilter.description: Filter your audience by the devices people have. We match a person if any of their devices meets the condition. To match people who have any device at all, set `field` to `id` and `operator` to `exists`.

field.description: The name of the device attribute you want to filter against. Use `id` to match people who have a device.

operator.description: Determine how to evaluate criteria against the field—`exists` returns results if a person has a device with the attribute; `eq` returns results if a person has a device with the attribute and the attribute has the `value` you specify.

value.description: The value you want to match for this device attribute. You must include a value if you use the `eq` operator.

inverse.description: Set to `true` to match people who *don't* have a device meeting the condition.

segmentTriggerCondition.title: segment
segmentTriggerCondition.description: Filter for people who belong to a segment.

attributeTriggerCondition.title: attribute
attributeTriggerCondition.description: Filter for people who have a profile attribute or a profile attribute value.

deviceAttributeTriggerCondition.title: device attribute
deviceAttributeTriggerCondition.description: Filter for people who have a device, or a device with a particular attribute value.

nestedNotTriggerFilter.title: not
nestedNotTriggerFilter.description: Returns people who don't match the condition inside it. `not` takes a single object, not an array. That object can be one condition, or an `and` or `or` group when you want to exclude people who match a combination of conditions.

complexTriggerFilter.title: Filter
complexTriggerFilter.description: Filter people with `and`, `or`, and `not` groups made from `segment`, `attribute`, and `device_attribute` conditions.

notTriggerFilter.title: not
notTriggerFilter.description: Returns people who don't match the condition inside it. `not` takes a single object, not an array. That object can be one condition, or an `and` or `or` group when you want to exclude people who match a combination of conditions.

triggerFilter.title: Filter
triggerFilter.description: Use `and`, `or`, and `not` to combine segment, attribute, and device attribute conditions. The top-level object accepts one property; nest groups for complex filters.

filter.description:
Narrows your audience to the people who also match one or more conditions. Use it to send to "these people, but only the ones who…". For example, you can send a push broadcast to a list of IDs (recipients) and skip the people who don't have a device (filter).

We check `filter` when the broadcast sends. An empty `ids`, `emails`, or `per_user_data` list falls back to the broadcast's saved audience, which you can't narrow, so sending `filter` with an empty list returns a `422`. The filter doesn't raise the limits on your list: we look up every identifier you send before we apply it.

machine_clicked.description: The number of `clicked` emails attributed to machines—security scanners, bot user agents, known proxy services, and repetitive click patterns. This metric is reliable starting April 20, 2025. [Learn more](/messaging/metrics/analytics/#delivery-metrics).

link_untracked.description: The number of emails delivered with link tracking inactive for any reason. We subtract these from the click-rate denominator.

tracking_consent_granted.description: The number of people who granted consent to email open tracking in the period.

tracking_consent_denied.description: The number of people who denied consent to email open tracking in the period.

metric.description: A device opened an in-app message. Because messages appear automatically when a person opens your app (to the right page if using page rules), "opened" is essentially an "impression"—a person saw your message.

The payload includes a `tracked_response` key containing the *Action Name* of the component the person clicked/tapped. [Learn more about tracked responses and action names](/journeys/channels/in-app/metrics/#tracked-responses).

If your workspace supports multiple identifiers, this object contains `cio_id` plus each enabled identifier—`id`, `email`, and (if enabled) `phone`. Each of these can be null when the person doesn't have that identifier set.

Otherwise, if your workspace only supports ID, this object just contains the `id` of the person the event represents.
